title: I liked the ridiculous scenes in Malignant (2021), but I struggle to see how it pays homage to giallo films

commenti.body: I think Malignant is the better version of the "wannabe Giallo but not actually a Giallo" compared to Last Night in Soho that just feel like a toothless 13 year old boys version of Giallo. I don't know I think some people watch Giallo and think it's only cool music, cool colors, cool kills and things happening really fast, but I feel as though there's much more to the genre than what Malignant, LNiS, and some of these other new "giallo" inspired movies give us.

His leather outfit and over-the-top bladed weapon are traditional giallo tropes as are her visions and connection to the killer. The twist itself is also a fairly giallo moment. There’s a good podcast episode about this movie on Best Little Horror House in Philly that goes into it a bit

I think the Giallo influences were earlier in the film, before the big reveal. From that point on it was just a Troma/Frank Henenlotter style farce. 

Things like set design, use of the color red, “black gloved killer”, was more noticeable in the first two acts before shit just went completely off the rails. Which I loved for the record haha.

I think the giallo influence was more on the aesthetic rather than the story. The trench coat and blade, the chase scene with the detective, the killer leaving threatening messages.

I actually knew nothing about it when I saw it in theaters. I was sold based on seeing the Argento style poster and that it was directed by James Wan. Only afterwards did I hear him talking about a giallo influence which, in hindsight, might’ve just been his way of saying “This is not the kind of movie you’re expecting from me.”
